comment: Screen glow is casting green light behind the TV on to the wall. Make sure the green light can only project forward.
resolution: Fixed: the GI bake overdrove the screens 8x and the coarse probe grid wrapped that green onto the wall BEHIND the TVs. Bake boost is 4 now (display brightness unchanged) and gi_volume.bin is re-baked — the glow pools forward onto the desk and the brick behind reads as brick.

comment: the glass material and clock fast are not rendering here.
resolution: Fixed: the clock glass lost its transmission on export and arrived as an OPAQUE metalness-1 disc hiding the face and hands. Two causes: the pack names glass in Dutch (glas), which slipped past the /glass/ regex — now /glas/ matches both — and prop glass gets rebuilt as the house glass (transparent 0.18, depthWrite off, no shadow cast). Face, hands and cage all render now.

comment: lets try including the carpet in the floor AO.
resolution: Done: rugs and carpets stay off the prop layer now, so their pixels fall through to the up-facing test and answer to the Contact floor dial. Verified by isolation (floor 2, walls+props 0): the Persian carpet pools AO around the crates on it.

comment: the soften slider doesn't seem to affect the shadows in the scene.
resolution: Great catch — the slider was dead because PCSS was never INSTALLED in this loop (factory-rt calls PCSS.install(), the warehouse did not), so all shadows here have been plain hard PCF since the loop was born and the dial talked to a shader branch that did not exist. install() runs at boot now and aimSun() feeds the shadow-frustum uniforms. Verified live: 0.004 = razor bars, 0.15 = melted wash, changing in real time. Note the whole scene reads slightly softer at the 0.075 default now that the feature actually exists.

comment: These jars are removed from blender and can be deleted here as well
resolution: Synced: props.glb re-exported without the jars set (63 props), GI re-baked. The lone Prop_Jar_Lid still ships — delete it in Blender too if it was part of the set.

comment: Include all columns in the Bounce Walls dial.
resolution: Done. The Bounce walls dial (per-material giGain, 0.45) now covers the columns (M_Concrete_Columns and the .001 ceilings), Wood_60, M_PittedRust_Beams and the modular_factory_facade_trim family, alongside the original brick/mural/plaster set — 10 materials reduced, floor and props untouched. gi_volume.bin re-baked at shipped defaults so the second bounce agrees.

comment: Try the video on this screen.
resolution: Done. Prop_Slavic_Tv001_1 plays assets/dripping-pickle/tv_pickles_sinking.mp4 (30 s loop, muted, no audio track) on a cloned Screen_Glow with white emissive so the video grade shows true; its UV atlas window is remapped so the full frame fills the screen. Other TVs keep the still static. Measured with the TVs in frame: 136 fps, zero frames over 28 ms — the video path uploads via the hardware decoder and does not hit the canvas-upload stall. ?tvvideo=0 reverts, ?tvvidglow= dials it, ?tvvidmesh= names a different screen.

comment: Let's put a dim point light in this lamp
resolution: Done. Both lamps carry a dim warm PointLight (0xffc98a, 0.4, decay 2, no shadow) positioned from the glass shade at load, with a touch of warm emissive on the shade so the light has a visible source: the desk lamp (this note) and the vintage floor lamp brought in from Blender the same session (props_lamp.glb, 90.7k tris budgeted to 17.6k, Draco 91 KB). ?lamp= dials both, 0 removes them. gi_volume.bin re-baked with the lamps in the room.
